newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:

- As a new Congress convenes on Tuesday vowing to cut taxes, tame Medicare and balance the federal budget, many believe the elements of success are aligned for the first time in years, but only if lawmakers can first deal with ethical issues involving campaign finance and Speaker Newt Gingrich.
- Newt Gingrich is to return to the Capitol on Monday and conduct his counteroffensive in person as he seeks to save his job as House Speaker.
- Football fans are rubbing their eyes after the Carolina Panthers beat the venerable Dallas Cowboys 26-17 on Sunday.

- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met covertly in the pre-dawn darkness on Sunday, but failed to either keep the meeting secret or to overcome remaining hurdles to a Hebron deal.

- The United States government intends to request a waiver of diplomatic immunity in the case of a diplomat from the former Soviet republic of Georgia involved in a fatal car accident in Washington late on Friday night.
- Harry Helmsley, New York's preeminent real estate investor, died Saturday in Scottsdale, Ariz., at 87.
- The federal government is shifting from developing nuclear arms to maintaining stockpiles in good condition and using computer simulations and other advanced techniques to insure their potency.
